title: Stabilize restored CI on the production Python runtime
description:
Restored GitHub Actions exposed deterministic failures in the production Python job and re-enabled a ruleset synchronization workflow whose administrative token is unavailable. The Python matrix also spends Actions minutes on a non-production runtime.

Expected behavior:
- Pull-request Python validation runs once on the production Python 3.11 runtime.
- The local Helm chart test provisions its repository metadata in an isolated test environment.
- Evaluation item lookup tests patch the supported explicit score resolver.
- Ruleset synchronization remains disabled until supported administrative authentication is available.
- Core CI, documentation, and release workflows remain enabled.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Live GitHub Actions evidence: both Python 3.11 and 3.12 jobs failed with the same three tests. The Helm test relied on developer-global repository configuration, two evaluation tests patched a dynamic package attribute that the explicit resolver intentionally rejects, and the Ruleset Sync job received an empty administrative token. Decision: keep core Actions enabled, validate only production Python 3.11, make the Helm test isolated, patch the supported resolver in tests, and defer ruleset authentication.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Implemented the CI stabilization. The production job now runs only Python 3.11; the Helm test provisions Bitnami metadata in isolated temporary configuration; evaluation tests patch the explicit score resolver; and Ruleset Sync is disabled until supported administrative authentication exists. Validation: red-first workflow contract failed in the two expected places, focused suite passes 9 of 9, Poetry lock validation and diff check pass, and a fresh isolated Python 3.11 environment completed the full CI command with 3,916 passed, 41 skipped, 3 expected failures, and no failures.
